A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpecPrune-VLA. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated and revised content.

before.justification: V2 reports original LIBERO evaluations, pruning ablations, hardware measurements, robustness experiments and real-robot results, including supplementary results in the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains original simulation and real-robot results and reports additional DB-OFT, CogACT, dynamic-scene and attention-backend evaluations.

M1.justification: The core pruning procedure, controller, equations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix A.1.4 adds an optional CogACT variant combining backbone pruning with static caching in the diffusion action expert, using cache interval 5; this changes that variant's inference procedure.

E1.justification: V3 expands SimplerEnv coverage from v2's UniVLA action-mode illustration to DB-OFT and CogACT visual-matching task sets. It also adds VLA-Arena dynamic-distractor and dynamic-obstacle scenarios. The original LIBERO suites, LIBERO-plus perturbations and four real-world tasks remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated unpruned π0 baseline disappears, while DB-OFT and CogACT become model baselines and Appendix A.1.5 introduces a FlashAttention baseline. The five acceleration comparators in the retained OpenVLA-OFT/LIBERO comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The replacement DB-OFT evaluation uses one camera view and ten backbone/action-expert denoising steps, versus the former two-view π0 setting. V3 also introduces CogACT-Base configurations, RTX 4090 simulation measurements and eager-versus-FlashAttention profiling over 256–2048 input tokens. These are new evaluation settings, not demonstrated reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test robustness to dynamic distractors and obstacles, the benefit of adding action-expert caching, and attention-backend latency across input lengths. Existing component, global-attention, entropy-weighting, threshold and pruning-ratio ablations remain; removing duplicate appendix displays does not remove those analyses.

E5.justification: V3 removes v2 Table 12 and Appendix A.5.3's independent-seed discussion and mean-plus-or-minus-half-range reporting, eliminating success-rate uncertainty evidence across all four LIBERO suites. Timing uncertainties remain in Table 9; its added sorting measurement follows the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 removes the π0 and repeated-run success-rate results and adds DB-OFT, CogACT, VLA-Arena, FlashAttention and RTX 4090 results. Table 1 reports DB-OFT success rates of 70.4% versus 70.1% with pruning and 1.44× speedup, although Section 7.4 says 1.34×. The retained OpenVLA-OFT and real-robot comparison tables preserve their values; the new evaluations do not establish same-setting gains over v2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, scoring and controller equations, FLOPs derivation and Fourier analysis are retained. Appendix A.3 clarifies range notation without changing the mathematical reasoning; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The training-free, two-level pruning contribution and headline 1.57× simulation and 1.70× real-world speedups remain. The introduction and conclusion replace π0-specific applicability with claims covering OpenVLA-OFT, DB-OFT and CogACT. The conclusion also changes the real-world accuracy claim from no compromise to negligible degradation.

C2.justification: V3 adds a specific limitation: high-velocity precision tasks may trigger inappropriate coarse pruning. It also explains CogACT's action-expert bottleneck and discusses short-input FlashAttention overhead and future long-input applicability. The central temporal-consistency interpretation remains, while the earlier repeated-run stability discussion disappears.

D1.justification: V3 documents DB-OFT's denoising procedure, CogACT-Base's 89M action expert, cache interval 5 and flash-attn version 2.5.5. It clarifies end-to-end timing boundaries for VLA-Cache comparisons. Conversely, v2's explicit OpenVLA-OFT encoder/backbone specifications are removed; the real-world training configuration remains.

R1.justification: V3 adds references including Dexbotic, VLA-Arena, FORA and VideoLLM, while removing several references associated with deleted model descriptions, including Gemma and flow matching. It adds positioning around FlashAttention compatibility, but Section 2 and the main novelty argument remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises parts of the introduction and conclusion, reorganizes appendix subsections, moves robustness discussion out of the main text and adds limitations, acknowledgments and an impact statement. Most methodological prose and the overall main-section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 substantially revises the profiling and overview figures, expands Table 1, merges the robot setup and task photographs, redraws robustness and velocity displays, and adds an attention-latency plot and evaluation tables. Duplicate appendix displays and the success-rate uncertainty table disappear; the final task visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: The added architecture, dynamic-scene and FlashAttention evaluations address useful generalization and efficiency questions, and the explicit high-velocity limitation improves qualification. However, removing the repeated-run success-rate evidence weakens support for negligible accuracy degradation. New reporting conflicts—including 1.44× versus 1.34× DB-OFT speedup and Table 5's SimplerEnv heading over LIBERO suite names—reduce clarity. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
